description: Implement the complete Meet Kelza section (investor question 3: why is Kelza different). This includes the HTML structure in index.html, CSS styles in a new meet-kelza.css file, and a MeetKelzaSection.js controller. The section has 4 parts: Product Philosophy (editorial principles), Ecosystem Visualization (interactive SVG), User Journey (narrative scroll-triggered flow), and a Transition bridge to the next section.
steps: Create css/meet-kelza.css following the pattern from css/why-section.css. Use BEM naming with .meet-kelza prefix. Include: (1) Section container with opacity:0/translateY hidden by default, revealed by .meet-kelza--visible. (2) Part 1 - Philosophy: full-width editorial statements with large typography (clamp-based fluid sizing), generous spacing. (3) Part 2 - Ecosystem: centered SVG layout with interactive hover/focus states on each module node, connection lines between nodes. (4) Part 3 - User Journey: vertical flow with step cards, each hidden by default and revealed via .meet-kelza__element--revealed class on [data-reveal] elements. (5) Part 4 - Transition bridge: single centered statement. (6) Reduced motion media query disabling all transitions and showing content immediately. (7) Responsive breakpoints at 640px, 768px, 1024px. Use only CSS variables from variables.css.

of why-section and BEFORE . Structure: (1) Section wrapper with class='meet-kelza-section' aria-label='Meet Kelza - Why Kelza is different' aria-hidden='true'. (2) Container div. (3) Part 1 - Philosophy: h2 heading + series of

editorial principle statements (use placeholder text in brackets like [Friendship before followers.]). (4) Part 2 - Ecosystem: h3 heading + inline SVG with central Kelza node and 9 surrounding module nodes (Discover, Match, Chat, Communities, Marketplace, Creator, Events, AI Companion, Trust & Safety). Each node must have role='img' aria-label, tabindex='0', and a visually hidden description element. Include connection lines from center to each module. (5) Part 3 - User Journey: h3 heading + ordered series of step elements with data-reveal attributes showing: New User, Find Interests, Meet People, Build Trust, Real Conversations, Communities, Friendships, Creator Economy, Long-term Engagement. (6) Part 4 - Transition bridge: p element with placeholder text.

Create js/sections/MeetKelzaSection.js following the WhySection.js pattern exactly. Export a class MeetKelzaSection with: constructor that gets element by id 'meet-kelza-section', _setupObserver() that observes all [data-reveal] children with IntersectionObserver (same thresholds and rootMargin as WhySection), _handleIntersections() that adds 'meet-kelza__element--revealed' class, reveal() that removes aria-hidden and adds 'meet-kelza--visible' class then calls _setupObserver(), hide() that reverses, isVisible(), and destroy(). Keep no function >60 lines, no class >400 lines.
Add @import './meet-kelza.css'; to css/main.css immediately after the @import './why-section.css'; line.

Update js/app.js: import { MeetKelzaSection } from './sections/MeetKelzaSection.js'; at the top with other imports, instantiate and call reveal() inside the DOMContentLoaded handler after whySection.reveal().
